summary: HSM-backed salt rotation during long-lived stream causes mismatched idempotency hashes and duplicate tool invocations across Python/TS/Go SDKs
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports duplicated external tool executions after a reconnect that occurs concurrently with a hardware-backed idempotency salt rotation. This is a private deployment using an HSM-backed key manager where salt rotations are performed automatically every 24h.

Impact:
- Multiple duplicate downstream webhook/tool executions observed (billing/side-effects).
- Affects long-lived streaming sessions that span a salt rotation window.
- Customer observed 2-3 duplicate callback executions per affected session.

Environment:
- Private deployment (VPC) with HSM KMS integration.
- SDKs in use: Python client v1.9.2, TypeScript client v0.12.0, Go client v0.8.7.
- Region: us-east.

Steps to reproduce (high level):
1) Start a long-lived streaming session that issues an external tool/function call which triggers a downstream webhook (e.g., payment capture).
2) Force a reconnect by throttling the client connection (or trigger a token refresh).
3) Rotate idempotency salt in HSM (customer reproducer rotates salt mid-session).
4) Resume stream; server and SDKs disagree on per-request idempotency hashing, leading to duplicate tool invocation.

Observed behavior:
- When rotation happens during reconnect, the server accepts what client believes to be a retry as a new request (new hash).
- Downstream webhook receives multiple identical execution requests.
- SDK logs show the client re-sending the tool call; server logs show distinct idempotency-hash values for what the client believes is the same logical operation.

Expected behavior:
- Retries and reconnects should be treated as the same logical operation when the client indicates it is a retry (idempotency scope preserved). Salt rotation should not invalidate in-flight retry semantics until apps can observe success/failure.

Customer-provided logs (sanitized):
- client-python: "INFO stream: sending func_call idempotency_key=op-492a; header-salt=base64:AQAB..."
- client-go: "WARN stream: reconnecting; new-session-salt not yet attached"
- server: "INFO req: computed idemp_hash=sha256(op-492a|salt-v2)"
- server (earlier): "INFO req: computed idemp_hash=sha256(op-492a|salt-v1)"

Workaround applied by customer:
- Temporarily disabled automated salt rotation window for the private deployment.
- Implemented an application-level confirmation callback to deduplicate downstream effects for critical operations.

Notes:
- Customer reported this first on 2026-03-09; replicated in staging on 2026-03-10 with an HSM simulator.
- They rely on HSM rotation policy for compliance; disabling rotation is not a long-term option.
investigation:
Initial triage performed by Support: reproduced in staging by forcing a salt rotation during an active streaming session. Behavior differs across SDKs:
- Python SDK attaches idempotency-salt at request creation and preserves per-request id field consistently across reconnects.
- TS SDK currently swaps the global salt asynchronously on rotation; if a reconnect happens in the swap window the outgoing headers can be missing or have the new salt unpredictably.
- Go SDK reuses a per-connection derived salt and on reconnect computes hash using the new global salt in some code paths due to non-atomic swap in the http2 header injector.

Hypothesis:
- Mid-session rotation + non-atomic swap of the salt value in SDKs causes computed idempotency hashes to diverge between the originally sent request and the retry, so the server treats retry as distinct.

What we've tried:
- Reproduced using HSM emulator and a controlled rotation pulse.
- Instrumented SDKs to log exact salt value used per-request.
- Confirmed server calculates different hashes matching the new/old salt values.

Next steps (short term):
- Advise customer to apply runbook: temporarily pause rotation during maintenance windows for long-lived sessions and enable application-level dedupe for critical side-effects.
- Provide a quick-fix guidance: set an explicit idempotency_key in the tool-call metadata so server can treat requests equal independent of salt rotation.

Next steps (engineering):
- Patch SDK-TS and SDK-Go to perform atomic salt swap for any in-flight session or attach session-scoped salt headers derived from a rotation-epoch token. PRs opened: see related_github_prs.
- Add e2e test that simulates salt rotation during reconnect to prevent regressions.
- Add runbook to Confluence and link in ticket.
current_status_update: 2026-03-12: Eng has started work on SDK-TS and SDK-Go fixes; SDK-Python confirmed to be already tolerant but will add more tests. Customer is applying temporary dedupe callback while we patch. Working on internal rollback/patch plan for private deploy customers who cannot disable rotation.
comments: 2026-03-09 - Priya Nair (Support): Acknowledged receipt and requested sanitized logs and exact SDK versions.
2026-03-10 - Frostbyte SRE (customer): Provided logs and a reproducer script that toggles salt via the HSM emulator. Confirmed duplicates for 12/20 runs.
2026-03-10 - Liam O'Connell (Support/Eng): Reproduced in staging with HSM emulator. Scoped to salt swap race across SDKs. Opening engineering follow-up.
2026-03-11 - Eng (sdk-ts): Noted non-atomic global swap in lib/crypto/salt_manager.ts; drafting atomic-swap patch.
2026-03-11 - Eng (sdk-go): Observed header injector re-use; proposing to add per-session salt header until rotation epoch boundary. Will reference PR when ready.
2026-03-12 - Priya Nair (Support): Sent customer temporary dedupe recommendations and sample middleware to add idempotency_key in tool metadata.
2026-03-12 - Frostbyte SRE: Confirmed they applied the middleware and observed zero duplicates in 50 runs while awaiting SDK patches.
